steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: I have already dismissed all the servants in the citadel. These footsteps, then...

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: ...Your Highness.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Ah, it's you. Did you need something?

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: You aren't going to ask how I returned?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: No, I won't. You came back, and that's all that matters, my loyal servant.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Besides, I have a fairly good idea of what sort of guest you can bring me.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Has the curfew started?

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: Just now.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Then you could say that my orders have been followed.

a.text: ...failure...

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Failure?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Na Saoirsí is here. I am here. What failure?

a.text: ...escape...

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: The deadline is Samhain. Surely the black mist remembers this, even if it's hardly known for being a good listener.

a.text: ...unsurprising...
...disappointing...
...unacceptable...

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Am I meant to understand something from these few words?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Or perhaps... you, too, prefer the directness of Arts and destruction to the imprecision of language?
No sooner do the words leave Eblana's lips than gleaming branches thrust forth from the dark mist, reaching for her throat.
At the same time, her spear penetrates the thick mist. Purple fire is faintly visible from within; she could burn it away to nothingness with a thought.
But the branches never find Eblana's throat, and her purple flames never ignite.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Samhain.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: By the time the sun rises on the day after Samhain, the outcome will be plain for all to see.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: So... why don't we dispense with these meaningless bluffs?
Eblana's spear still impales the mist, but the branches before her throat disappear a moment later, as do the flames at the tip of her spear.
The dark mist dissipates.

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: Your Highness...

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: You're still here.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Did you need something else? Is this about Dublinn?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: There are only the two of us here. I will permit you to speak that word again, my most loyal servant.

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: Thank you, but there is no need.

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: Spectres are but spectres, even if they helped found a nation. There is no place for ghosts in the history books.

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: But I worry about my colleagues who stayed behind that day, as I did... Where are they? Could they mean you harm?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: No need to worry. Even if there were, that is no reason for you to risk staying here.

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: ...I saw a scene of chaos on my way back.

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: It was bedlam. People were fighting over the tiniest things... sometimes nothing at all. While others seemed to be stuck where they stood, like statues.

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: Just like the spectres who fought the Victorians with us.

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: Will they fade into darkness too?

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: This is Na Saoirsí, the Red Dragon's Lair, the capital of Tara. Anything that happens here will have repercussions across the nation.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: No, it won't.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: You don't sound convinced.

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: Your Highness... I...

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: At the end of the day, I have just one question.

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: One question I pray you will answer.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Very well. I will forgive your imprudence.

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: (Takes a deep breath)

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: Your Highness Eblana, that future...

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: That future you promised Dublinn, you promised Tara, that future where all Tarans could freely write their own dreams...

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: Was it all a lie?
The Brigadier cannot stop himself from trembling. The fear that had lurked in his heart for days overcomes him.
It is not because he fears his own end. He is not afraid of being swallowed by the dark mist like his colleagues, or of invoking the red dragon's wrath.
He fears that he will hear an answer he dare not consider.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: It was true, every word of it.

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: Your Highness...

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: I have answered your question, Brigadier.
The red dragon's voice seems ethereal, feeble even, but it leaves no room for questioning.
It is the voice that has led the man to victory countless times, and so he slowly straightens his back.

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: Then I trust you.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Perhaps... Or perhaps you simply have no other choice.

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: Often have you chosen a path that seemed baffling, impossible even. But it always ends up leading us closer to our dream. Of that I have no doubt.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Such deep trust is indeed worthy of my gratitude.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: However, I do not require you to maintain order within Na Saoirsí.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: If you managed to return from the Dark Woods, then you should return there now.

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: Until Samhain has passed?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Until Samhain has passed.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Or...

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: 'I stepped into the dark woods one morn, calling to the mists of hoar'...

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: Your Highness?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Do you hear the song coming from beyond the woods?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Hardly a day has passed since you left... Fine work, Loughshinny.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Is that what's been happening in the city?!

spans.text: what's been happening in the city?!

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Reed, your sister... what is she planning?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I don't know.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Someone once told me that her plans would only ever be beneficial to Tara. Now, though, I can trust neither her nor the one who made that promise.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Are you still not going to help her, wakewoman?

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: She came for a funeral, and we will only accept her for that.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: I have learned of the deeds of the departed.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Bring the knots and wreaths and come outside. The funeral is about to begin.
The people set aside their differences and stand up in silence.

a.text: I stepped into the dark woods one morn, calling to the mists of hoar♪
I trod upon the road, heading out to war♪
No pipes a-singing, nor battle drums a-roar♪
Only the bells behind me, through dew and fog their rings do soar♪

steps.text: The wakemen sing softly, each attending to their own duty.
Some adorn the coffin with knots and wreaths.
Some lay firewood and kindling around it.
Some distribute candles to the attending refugees as they continue to sing.
Tiny lights begin to sway throughout the camp.
Loughshinny has a candle too, which she carefully lifts in front of her chest.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Excuse me...

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Go ahead.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: I didn't know the departed, and don't really have much to say... But where I grew up, people talked freely at funerals.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Certainly. This is how Tarans honor the departed.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Life should be celebrated, even after its end. The joy of the living is consolation to the dead. You are free to talk amongst each other.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: I also made some snacks...

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Please feel free to share them. We will also provide refreshments later.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: However, we must request that you exercise restraint, considering that Mr. Culann died before his time, and under unfortunate circumstances.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: We must also ask you to follow our instructions during the fire-returning ceremony.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Understood.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Is this how your folks hold funerals, Moran?

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: We didn't have all these rites and ceremonies. All we did was keep watch through the night. No clue what this 'fire-returning' thing is either.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Guess we just follow their instructions.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Have you ever been part of a ceremony like this, Reed?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: I see...

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: You mean...

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Loughshinny has found the wakemen. The hero's funeral has begun.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: 'I stepped into the dark woods one morn, calling to the mists of hoar; I trod upon the road, heading out to war'... Do you know this song?

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: You already know the answer.

steps.name: The Brigadier
steps.text: I led the young into battle with it more than a few times.

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: Who is it? Who's singing?

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: Why is it that I still hear that song here at the site of the old capital, even after escaping the Dark Woods?

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: Or am I still stuck in the woods?!

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: No... no, the sound is coming from the furnace at the center of the ruins.

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: Such a beautiful tune...

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: No pipes a-singing, nor battle drums a-roar...

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: Only the bells behind me... through dew and fog their rings do soar...

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: I should go back...

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: Now I see... what I truly want...

steps.name: 'The Singer'
steps.text: Besides... do I really deserve... to escape Na Saoirsí?

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: Here, Emma, today's bread.

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: Thanks for sharing your food in times like these.

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: You shared with me before. Just returning the favor.

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: But... why do you keep staring at the bread in my hand like that?

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: (Mutters) Control yourself... control yourself...

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: (Mutters) She's Emma... the one who shared bread with you... you must help her... you must—

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: (Deep breath) I'm fine, Emma.

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: I-I just meant to say, you've been bedridden for so long. There'll be tough times ahead.

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: 'No pipes a-singing, nor battle drums a-roar'...

steps.name: Anxious Resident
steps.text: Why are you singing that?

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: Someone's singing... in the distance...

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Friends of the departed, please present your eulogy before the fire-returning ceremony begins.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Reed?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I... I have a eulogy here, written by Nemos. May I read it?

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Of course. Go ahead.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: 'Dear Culann...'

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: A letter?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: 'Culann, perhaps it won't be long before I join you...'

a.text: Culann, perhaps it won't be long before I join you—before I become a slave of the purple flame, before I turn to ash.
Perhaps there won't be anyone to free me from an afterlife of eternal torment.
But I've never forgotten what you said to me.
You said you wanted to be a hero. You asked me to let you become one.
You said Na Saoirsí needed a hero for the postwar days, one who belonged only to us. Neither Dublinn nor soldier.
You said that nearly everyone in the city had lost something important in the war, be it a partner, a child, or a future.
Without a hero, an exemplar to understand them and fight for their rights, one who would also set them right should they go astray...
Without that, they wouldn't have anything to hold onto when the war ends, when they have no one left to hate.
I agreed and assented to your request.
You took Theo in, and helped the people who'd lost their livelihoods.
You thought everything was on the right path, and so you proposed the statue. You became fully immersed and took on a great burden.
By the time you realized... it was too late.
Now, it is my turn to carry this burden, one too heavy for any single person to bear.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: '...Now, it is my turn to carry this burden, one too heavy for any single person to bear.'

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: 'Farewell, Culann. Slán leat. Or should I say, Slán go fóill.'

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: 'May we meet again...'

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: 'in the warm flames.'
As she finishes, a flame is thrown into the kindling surrounding the coffin, igniting the firewood.
The crowd gathers around the bonfire, following the instructions of the wakemen.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Witness that the departed has found peace in flames. He shall no longer wander the mortal realm.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Place your candle as close to the fire as possible, or throw it in directly. Return the fire to the departed.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: If you have anything to say to the departed, say it aloud to the flame. Be it praise or reproach, they are the memories that will console the departed at journey's end.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Once you have returned the fire, please remain to keep watch over his soul, until the fire has gone out.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Let us begin.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Slán leat. May you find rest, stranger—

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: deceiver and hero.
Moran bends down and places her candle by the fire. The licking flames swallow it in an instant, almost burning her hand.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Do you want to come closer to the fire, Reed?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: If there's anyone here who doesn't deserve to pay respects to Culann, it would be me.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: You couldn't have saved him.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Moran?

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: There was no place for him in the Red Dragon's Lair from the moment he made the choice to truly become a hero.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: You should return the fire to him.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Ashes to ashes, dust to dust. Let the dead rest with our memories, as life goes on.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Return the fire...

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Let the dead rest with our memories... as life goes on?
While Loughshinny is lost in thought, the others continue to return their fire and then sit down some distance from the bonfire, until she is the only one left with a candle in her hand.
She walks forward in silence, and tosses the candle into the blazing bonfire.
The dead are gone.
All their ambition, obsession, realization and desperation turn to fading smoke and silent ash in the flames.
